key_insight: Progressive Multimodal Alignment (PMA) prevents projector-level forgetting in continual multimodal instruction tuning by expanding projector capacity only when new visual-language shifts require it, while keeping the original projector as a stable anchor.
engineering_relevance: For multimodal AI systems used in engineering workflows, PMA improves long-term robustness to changing data and instructions without requiring full-model retraining or large parameter growth.
method: Detect multimodal distribution shifts with a lightweight representation descriptor.
Add projector experts progressively only when needed.
Use an expandable router to combine expert outputs while retaining the pretrained projector as an alignment anchor.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over prior state-of-the-art methods on two recent MCIT benchmarks and broad effectiveness across multiple MLLM backbones.
watch_item: Because PMA adds routing and expert-expansion logic, performance may depend on reliable shift detection and careful management of added projector parameters in deployment.
paper_title: Progressive Multimodal Alignment for Continual Instruction Tuning
